market_context.summary: The single most important frame today inverts the usual read: the Fed is HIKING, not cutting. September's FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike since 2023 and unanimous, and the minutes released around Oct 7 record 16 of 18 officials expecting at least one more 25bp increase in 2026. Expectations have migrated from October to December — Kalshi prices the Oct 28 hike at 16c and the Dec 9 hike at 74c — which backs out to roughly an 82% chance of a December hike conditional on an October hold, near-certainty about a specific action four major data releases away from a committee with two named members publicly asking to wait. Fed projections put 2026 PCE at 3.7% headline / 3.4% core with no return to 2% until 2029. The long end sits 134bp above the funds rate at 5.22% with CPI re-accelerating (+0.40% MoM in August, ~4.9% annualized) and unemployment drifting up 4.1% to 4.2%: a term-premium, stagflation-lean tape rather than a soft-landing one. Note the tension the event market is pricing — a hike WITHOUT an inflation re-acceleration (Above 0.4% MoM at 16c, Above 4.0% YoY at 25c), so the hike case rests on the level of inflation rather than its momentum. Consequences traded off today: duration is the wrong side, every rate-cut-dependent and long-duration equity thesis carries a higher bar than it did last week, real assets and energy are favoured, and crypto is a liquidity asset into tightening. Refining is the tape's confirmed leadership (3-2-1 crack spread ~$69.72/bbl, August's NY Harbor average the highest monthly value since 2006) and power is the second, but both are already owned. The week ahead is dense: Q3 earnings season opens Oct 13 with JPM/GS/C/WFC, September CPI lands Oct 14 08:30, PPI and retail sales Oct 15. Equity markets were closed all day Sunday, so every equity entry here is an order for the Monday Oct 12 open — on which the bond market is closed for Columbus Day.

watchlist.note: CUT from rank 1 (conviction 4, 3% — the only new risk in the report). The thesis rested on a premise that was already false when it was written. It claimed the season produced "no hurricanes ... with no US landfall for the first time in ten years": Hurricane Isaias, the season's first and the latest first Atlantic hurricane on record, formed Oct 7-8, reached Category 3 on Oct 9 and made US Gulf Coast landfall between Mobile AL and Pensacola FL in the early hours of Sat Oct 10, with a storm-surge warning from the mouth of the Mississippi to Steinhatchee FL. NHC public advisory 19, 04:00 CDT Oct 11, has it post-tropical over Tennessee. Research sourced the no-hurricane claim to a Verisk blog explicitly dated "as of 2026-10-06" and never consulted the NHC primary, so the single fact the idea turned on was three days stale at publication. The cat-light Q3 mechanic does survive — Q3 closed Sept 30 and no later storm changes that print. What does not survive is the catalyst instruction built on it: "hold through Oct 16 rather than trimming, the catastrophe-loss risk is already resolved, because Q3 closed Sept 30." The stock trades the live Q4 event, not the Q3 income statement — Isaias is an estimated $4-6B industry insured loss (BMS Group, Gallagher Re, both pre-landfall), it is unpriced in the Friday Oct 9 close every level in the row was derived from, and Q4 cat load is now the first question on the Oct 16 call. The levels are what made it unfixable rather than merely wrong: entry 364-369.5 and the 352 stop (2.32 ATR on a 6.4657 ATR) are pre-event numbers, and a limit at or below 369.5 sits above any plausible gap-down open, so it is an unconditional fill into the first session that prices the storm. Repairing it needs a post-event price, which does not exist on a Sunday, and inventing one is the one thing this pipeline forbids.
watchlist.trigger: Re-arm only after Monday Oct 12 trades and the storm is priced, then re-derive entry, stop and target from a post-Oct-12 close and a post-event ATR, and state a Q4 cat-load view explicitly instead of calling the cat risk resolved. The catalyst itself is intact and confirmed: Oct 16 bmo, consensus EPS 6.8423 on revenue ~$11.49B, verified on a 7-day refetch of the earnings calendar. Brokers read Isaias as mid-single-digit billions and not enough to move US property capacity or the soft market, and the Q3 cat line really is clean, so a TRV long may well be a better idea on Tuesday than it was on Friday. It simply cannot be published on Friday's levels and a false landfall claim.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH COMPLETED — the research phase wrote a RESEARCH COMPLETE block plus an addendum at 06:45 ET, so nothing here is reconstructed from a truncated log and `truncated` is false. 

WHY ONLY ONE NEW IDEA. This is a management day, not an idea day, and the count is not being padded. Of six recommendations, ONE is new risk (TRV), one is a hold on a position opened Oct 9 (XLF), three are exits, and one is a target amendment. Research rejected GS, AA, EQT, NRG, TLN, CB, WRB, VLO/MPC/PSX, a short /MBT and two Fed/CPI event-contract complexes rather than writing them up thin. The reasons were specific: the tape's leadership is refining and power and the book already owns both (XLE, DINO, CEG); the cheap cyclicals are cheap at their lows with no base to lean a stop on; and the macro event contracts are priced to the cent. The track record was applied rather than noted — 2/15 overall, 0/8 on closed stock ideas and 0/4 on conviction 2 — so the one new stock idea carries four distinct kinds of evidence and CCJ was cut to conviction 2 at 1% rather than defended. 

EDITORIAL CORRECTION, DISCLOSED. Research captured the three exits (LCII, LULU, NKE) with `direction: sell`, meaning "the action is to sell". Published that way they would have done the opposite of what research decided, and this was verified against state/open_positions.json rather than assumed: merge_report keys one live position per (symbol, direction), and the book holds LIVE SHORT positions in LULU (entry 100.61, target 77.00, stop 112.00, +6.1%) and NKE (entry 38.40, target 32.10, stop 41.00, +9.6%). A published LULU/NKE `sell` would have amended those two profitable, properly-stopped shorts — overwriting their targets to the current price and their stops to null — while leaving the losing longs open and unstopped, and an LCII `sell` would have opened a fabricated new short. All three are therefore published as `direction: buy` with `horizon: long_term`, matching the live long each one closes, with the stop moved to Friday's close (78.30 / 94.50 / 34.71) — the level at which research says the thesis is already invalid, and the fix for the actual defect, which is that these three positions never had a stop at all.
